demographics.trauma_type: Unexpected or traumatic death of a loved one

Maladaptive Strategies.value: go over and over why the event happened to me
try hard not think about the trauma
Anything that reminds me of someone I have lost

Threat.value: Taking too many risks or doing things that could cause you harm
Having strong negative feelings such as fear, horror, anger, guilt, or shame
Suddenly feeling or acting as if the stressful experience were actually happening again

Memory.value: Fragments of the memory appear suddenly without warning and then disappear
I feel like I am only remembering parts of what happened and the rest is missing
When I try to deliberately remember what happened I find it difficult to access the memory

issues.item: Rehearse Conversations: rehearse what to say before any interaction
issues.explanation: Several selected items imply a hypervigilance/physical-assault style threat profile (scanning exits, reacting to sudden movements, avoiding open spaces) that is hard to reconcile with the indexed trauma of unexpected death of a loved one. These items usually fit interpersonal violence, combat, or other danger-based trauma more than bereavement trauma.

issues.item: Avoid Open Spaces: Open or exposed spaces where I feel vulnerable
issues.explanation: 'Rehearse Conversations before any interaction' suggests prominent social-evaluative anxiety, but there are no corresponding threat or memory items about social humiliation, blame, or feared conversations about the death. It sits awkwardly with the rest of the profile and does not clearly connect to the active Memory→Threat→Strategies formulation.

issues.item: Avoid Open Spaces: Open or exposed spaces where I feel vulnerable
issues.explanation: These items imply a danger-based, assault-like or combat-like threat profile centered on physical attack and environmental vulnerability, which is hard to reconcile with the indexed trauma of unexpected death of a loved one.

issues.item: Scanning Exits: I scan for exits as soon as I enter any room or building
issues.explanation: The threat content is internally coherent with hypervigilance for interpersonal/physical danger, but that pattern is not clinically well matched to the rest of the profile, where memory items reflect disorganized recall of a death-related trauma rather than threat from current spaces, exits, or others' movements.

issues.item: Threat in Movements: Sudden movements by others put me immediately on guard
issues.explanation: 'Sudden movements by others put me immediately on guard' is more typical of interpersonal violence/combat threat cues and is hard to reconcile with a trauma of unexpected death of a loved one when the rest of the profile centers on grief-related memory disturbance rather than current danger from people.

vignette: Kofi had always been a man who thrived on control and precision, making a successful career for himself as a stock broker in New York City. But that all changed on a typical Monday morning two years ago, when he received the devastating news that his only child, 25-year-old daughter Ama, had died suddenly in a car accident on her way to work. Kofi was consumed by an unbearable grief, and as the days turned into weeks, and the weeks into months, he found himself struggling to make sense of the tragedy. As he tried to navigate his new reality without Ama, Kofi became increasingly preoccupied with questions about why this had happened to him. He would spend hours ruminating on every possible explanation, from fate to divine retribution, but no matter how hard he tried, he couldn't shake off the feeling of responsibility that weighed heavily on his shoulders. "What if I had been more involved in her life?" he would ask himself over and over again. In an attempt to cope with these unbearable thoughts, Kofi started to suppress any memories or emotions associated with Ama's passing, trying hard not to think about the trauma. However, this avoidance strategy only seemed to exacerbate his pain. Everyday objects, like the coffee mug Ama had given him for his birthday just a few months before her death, would suddenly bring back vivid memories of their time together, and Kofi would find himself becoming overwhelmed with emotion. He began to avoid anything that reminded him of Ama, including visiting places they used to go to together or even looking at old family photos. As the anniversary of Ama's passing approached, Kofi started to feel an intense sense of restlessness. He began taking more risks in his trading, hoping to prove to himself that he was still capable of controlling the world around him. But this only led to a series of losses, both financial and emotional, as he struggled with feelings of guilt, shame, and fear. "I'm losing everything," he would say to himself, "just like I lost Ama." Kofi also started experiencing flashbacks, where he would suddenly feel as if he was reliving the moment when he received the news about Ama's death. He would find himself in his car, driving home from work, and suddenly be transported back to that fateful day, with all the emotions and memories flooding back. Despite trying hard to remember what happened on the day of Ama's passing, Kofi found it incredibly difficult to piece together a complete picture. Fragments of memories would appear suddenly without warning, only to disappear just as quickly, leaving him feeling frustrated and disoriented. When he tried to deliberately recall the events leading up to her death, he found his mind going blank. As the months went by, Kofi's behavior became increasingly erratic, causing concern among his colleagues and friends. His isolation deepened, and he started to withdraw from social interactions, unable to bear the thought of facing the world without Ama by his side. It was only when Kofi's boss called him into her office, expressing worry about his declining performance and warning him that his job was at risk, that he realized he needed help. As he sat in his therapist's office for the first time, Kofi knew that he couldn't continue living like this – stuck in a cycle of grief, guilt, and avoidance. He hoped that therapy could help him find a way to confront his pain and learn to live with the loss of his beloved daughter Ama. With tears streaming down his face, Kofi whispered, "I just want to be able to remember her without feeling like I'm losing my mind."
